label: Agents write the code
title: Writing code by hand is becoming the exception
thesis: At the organisations furthest into agent use, agents now do most of the implementation, and writing code by hand is what needs explaining. Human work moves to directing agents, specifying tasks and building the tools that watch them, so people become a minority of the effort on a team.
construct: How much of the implementation effort in a software organisation is carried out by agents rather than people - agent-hours per human hour, share of merged code written by agents, whether hand-writing is the exception. Not the share of developers who use AI tools, tool satisfaction or market share, suggestions accepted, or output per developer, all of which rise while people still write most of the code.
currentPressure: Agent output is outrunning the systems around it (CI load, review queues, spend), and vendors report their own teams already working this way.

implications.statement: Where agents carry the implementation, human session time goes to waiting on, directing and instrumenting them: about 80% of interactive agent session time waits on a person, and meta-work on agent tools, specs and monitors rose from 10% to 22% of sessions in six months.

Whether engineers write code by hand stops being a personal habit and becomes an operating-model decision, with an engineer who finds themselves hand-writing treated as a sign the agent workflow needs fixing.
When agents log about three workdays for each human workday, headcount stops measuring a team's capacity and agent consumption becomes the larger part of what the team does.

evidence.note: OpenAI research org telemetry: 3.1 agent-workdays per human workday (from under 1 before June); over half of successful 4-8 hour tasks still needed at least one human intervention

Anthropic workforce data: employee-directed agents passed human hours in March 2026 and reached ~6x by August; commits per engineer ~5x six months earlier; ~80% of interactive agent session time spent waiting on a person
Claude Code team says Claude writes about 90% of the product's code; changes per day across Anthropic's monorepo from ~2,500 to 30,000+ (same sponsor as 2026-10-26-01, counts as one context)

37signals 'pencils down': agents are the normal way of building, hand-writing treated as a sign the workflow needs fixing, HEY being rebuilt by a small team with a Rust backend written by agents; one company, own keynote
Amazon pilot: in the better teams engineers wrote only 1-2% of the code directly and let the assistant run unattended for up to several hours

Pragmatic Engineer survey of 906 engineers: 56% report doing 70%+ of their engineering work with AI; self-reported share of work done with AI, including assisted use, so it shows pressure without showing agent authorship
Science study of 30M+ GitHub commits: ~29% of US Python functions AI-written by end 2024; function-level classifier on a 2024 cut-off, so a share of assisted code well short of a majority

JetBrains Developer Ecosystem Survey 2026, 15,000+ professional developers, May-July 2026, reweighted to the global population: agents fully generate ~47% of code on average, ~27% written fully by hand; over half write <20% manually; ~22% get >80% from agents; seniors lead; Europe/UK ~16% fully delegate vs 32-35% in East Asia. Self-reported in bands; vendor survey

reachRationale: Writing code by hand is now the minority practice across the field, not only at forerunners. JetBrains' 2026 survey of over 15,000 professional developers, weighted to represent developers worldwide, finds agents fully generate about 47% of their code on average and only about 27% is written entirely by hand; over half of developers write less than a fifth of their code manually, and senior developers lead the shift. The organisations whose tools most engineers use run most of their own implementation through agents, and established product companies such as 37signals have made hand-written code the exception. This changes what the field expects of a software engineer. Full delegation is still a minority, about a fifth of developers, and Europe lags: about 16% of European and UK developers get most of their code from agents, against a third in East Asia. The survey figures are self-reported estimates.
whatWouldChangeThis: Independent organisations with no vendor tie reporting that humans still write most merged code in agent-heavy teams
Human-intervention rates on multi-hour agent tasks staying above half, or rising
Forerunners reversing, as Meta did on its second restructuring wave, after measuring their own agent output
A measured share of merged code written by agents at mainstream delivery organisations staying near the 0-20% full-delegation range
